Definition: of Hebrew origin (H1403); Gabriel, an archangel:--Gabriel.
BiblicalUsage: Gabriel is the angel who stands in the presence of God, and Luke names him twice. He tells Zechariah in Luke 1:19 that he is Gabriel, sent to speak glad tidings, and in Luke 1:26 he is sent from God to Nazareth, to a virgin named Mary. The name means God is my strength, and he carries the greatest announcements in the Gospel.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Gabriel matters because he brings God's own words to men; he stood in the presence of God and was sent to speak, and I hold that the announcements he carried — a son to Zechariah, a Son to Mary — changed the world.
